coverage_rule: Two individual named characters and one direct relation supported by the estate's official Tombs synopsis only: Tenar/Arha and Ged Sparrowhawk. Ged is included solely for the contained Tombs conflict and is not a re-recording of SRC-035's Wizard attributes, teachers, peers, dragon encounter, or shadow crisis.
omissions: All A Wizard of Earthsea cohort records and all SRC-035-specific character facts except a concise overlap note for Ged.
All other contained novels, stories, essays, and the new story in the 2018 container; they require separate work-level witnesses.
All other Tombs characters, underground events, outcomes, true names, rituals, metaphysics, and later Earthsea consequences not directly stated in the official synopsis.
Graphic-novel, animated, television/miniseries, and any other adaptation continuities.
uncertainties: The 2018 book is a container with illustrations and supplementary material, not a newly unified narrative continuity. Charles Vess's commissioned/selected artwork is edition material and is not used as character-canon evidence.
This is an official-reference pass rather than a chapter/page primary-text pass; its character claims are restricted to the estate synopsis.
Tenar's imposed name Arha and title Eaten One are contextual identity claims, not a generic naming mechanic or a statement that a name grants control over a person.
The synopsis signals child removal, coercive religious office, isolation, theft/conflict, and danger in a labyrinth. Resolution and later-life spoilers are omitted.
evidence_basis: Simon & Schuster's official product record establishes the 2018 Saga Press container, contents, ISBN, and illustration credit. The Le Guin estate's official Tombs page is the sole evidence for the selected later-work character, title, treasure, and conflict claims.
